scenario: LCRS.4.2.1 and LCRS.6.6.1: `CallError` is `ttl`-scoped at 5_min, so an orphaned one leaves working memory 5 minutes after it is asserted. High half of the discriminating pair: identical to LCRS.4.2.1_callerror_ttl_alive until the clock stands at 5 min minus 1 ns, then it advances one further nanosecond onto the deadline and the fact is retracted ([LFAC.1.2], expiry at now >= deadline). The advance is a separate step so that the alive half's instant is reached here too. `seen` names `CallError` so the compiler injects the built-in schema. PATH PINNED: the built-in declaration in `dsc.builtins` (`builtin_schema("CallError", ...)`), lowered to the schema's TTL atom; libds and the Mercury runtime both take the deadline from the artefact. The break is a built-in schema of `ttl 24_h`: the fact is still live and the count is 1.
